sentences.text:
The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 27.05.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That, on 27.05.2024 at about 8.45 p.m., the petitioner being the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-EN-0587 was waiting to cross the Sulthan Palya Main Road, near Shanmugam hospital, R.T. Nagar, Bengaluru using indicators, at that time, all of a sudden the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-01-EG- 4251 came with high and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to Chaitanya hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 27.05.2024 to 31.05.2024.
He spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, hospitalization, food, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 40 years and was working in a Garments and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has suffered disability and he is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motor cycle.
Hence, the present claim petition.
3. After presentation of the petition, notice was issued to the respondent.
Despite of service of notice, the respondent has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and was placed exparte.
4. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following points arise for my determination :
POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proved that, on 27.05.2024 at about 8.45 p.m., the petitioner being rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-09-EN-0587 was waiting to cross the Sulthan Palya Main Road, near Shanmugam hospital,
R.T. Nagar, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EG-4251 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained injuries ?

2 2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
7.

My finding on the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Affirmative  Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Point No.3 :
POINT No.1:

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 27.05.2024.
9.
The petitioner stepped into the witness box and examined himself as PW-1.
On behalf of the petitioner, 13 documents were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0051/2024 of R.T. Nagar Traffic Police and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.
On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-01-EG-4251.
Ex.P.3 is the seizure mahazar wherein it reveals that, during investigation I.O. has seized the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.10 is the charge sheet filed by the R.T. Nagar Traffic police against one Mr. Mohammed Junaid who is none other than the rider of the offending vehicle.
On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
10. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This veiw receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

Ex.P.7 is the wound certificate wherein it reveals that,
the petitioner has sustained simple injuries in the road traffic accident.

Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that the accident in question had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EG-4251 and the petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.
Hence, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
11. POINT No.2:-
As stated above, the petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of rider of the offending motor cycle.

The petitioner contended that, he has sustained 1) Lacerated wound measuring 3x2x6cm deep Pala Naik R vs Abdul Raheem on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183725948/
3 present over left ankle and left heel and 2) injury to perineal retinaculam and perineal tendon.

sentences.text: He further stated that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Chaithanya hospital, Bengaluru and taken treatment as an inpatient from 27.05.2024 to 31.05.2024 and spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and incidental expenses and supposed to spent more amount in future.
12. I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
In the petition, the petitioner has contended that in the accident he has sustained injuries.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.7.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has suffered simple injuries.

Ex.P.11 is the discharge summary, wherein it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the hospital on 27.05.2024 and discharged on 31.05.2024.
13.
Ex.P.12 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.55,033/-.
On perusal of the medical bills, Sl.No.1 i.e. IPD bill/ receipt amounting to Rs.53,316/- was paid to the hospital by Vidal Health Insurance Pvt. Ltd.
Hence, it appears that the said final bill has already been paid by the health insurance company to the hospital.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for the amount claiming under the Sl.No.1 of Ex.P.12 medical bills.
Further, the petitioner has produced 7 medical bills i.e. Sl.No.2 to 8 amounting to Rs.3,229/-.
The said medical bills produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills of Rs.3,229/-.
14.
As per the medical documents it appear that, petitioner has suffered injuries and admitted to the hospital for treatment for a period of 5 days.

Considering the treatment taken for the injuries as an in patient, pain and sufferings, nourishment and diet food including medical bills amount, if Global compensation Rs.35,000/- is awarded it will be just and proper.

15. In the instant case, the respondent is the owner of the offending Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-EG- 4251.
On perusal of the contents of the charge sheet, it reveals that, on the date of accident there was no valid insurance to the offending vehicle.

Therefore, the respondent being owner is liable to pay the compensation of Rs.35,000/- to the petitioner with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, Point No.2 answered partly in the Affirmative.
16. POINT No. 3:

For the aforesaid reasons on Point No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.35,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
